notes: BASELINE WARNING: both sides were measured against upstream main 39658a9 with iii 0.22.1. This branch was later rebased onto tag v0.9.29 (2d38daf, iii-sdk pin 0.11.2), so the recorded baseline is no longer the branch's base and a re-measurement against v0.9.29 is outstanding. Do not quote these numbers as a v0.9.29 comparison.
Reproduction: npm run bench:memory-retention -- --url http://127.0.0.1:PORT --label LABEL --pid NODE_PID --pid III_PID --data-dir DATA_DIR
Isolated instances used ports 3311 and 3211 with separate HOME and data directories.
RSS sums the agentmemory Node process and its iii engine child; the committed harness samples /proc every 200ms and records data-dir growth.
This is a worst-case large-output synthetic/BM25/heuristic-graph workload with no LLM or embedding provider; it does not measure the full compress-embed-LLM graph path.
Upstream had not returned to baseline by the end of cycle two (settled RSS equaled its sampled maximum), so the growth reduction is the primary memory signal.
cycle_1, cycle_2, total_data_bytes and store_composition_after_two_cycles are computed by hand from the two per-run files each side emits; the harness itself only reports per-run primitives.
Structure-preserving payload truncation trades synthetic load throughput for metadata retention; the fork is 15.7% and 27.2% slower in these two cycles.
The fork still grows because iii file_based keeps a decoded in-memory representation; this change reduces client-side write amplification but does not replace the engine allocator.
